subject: Close the metabolism loop: quality, cost, latency, storage, and proof reuse must co-train scheduling

body.objective: Make ProviderGraph, MoneyGraph, ResourceGraph, ContextCompiler and ProofFrontier one feedback economy rather than adjacent services.
required_actions: For every completed epoch record provider/model, wall time, token/context pressure where available, bytes written, peak free-space delta, external spend or zero-cost classification, receipt/proof bytes, retry count, semantic outcome, and downstream reuse count.

Create a FactorValidityEnvelope for learned routing factors so provider/resource/cost conclusions expire when model version, provider policy, schema, task class, resource envelope, or architecture owner changes.
Feed validated factors into admission/provider selection: expected semantic value per dollar, second, GiB-write, and context token. Never optimize raw throughput over evidence quality.
Count proof reuse as negative future cost: a SolvedInvariant that suppresses five reruns is economically more valuable than a cheap repeated epoch.
Run counterfactual backtests over recent Run8 receipts: compare actual schedule against at least two alternative schedules and report avoided/reintroduced failures without mutating history.
Expose KnownNonCause when a provider quota, disk floor, schema bug, or transport defect—not task semantics—caused failure, so learning never poisons task fitness.
body.output: One compact metabolic receipt plus updated scheduling factors, with no silent permanent learning from stale evidence.
